estimate.damage_summary: A nearby atmospheric discharge caused an overvoltage on the building’s electrical installation, physically damaging a speaker system and TV. A technician later attended to confirm the surge failure and check the wiring.
estimate.policy_notes: The damaged appliances fall under the electrical-appliance sub-limit of EUR 5,000 including VAT per event. Because no overvoltage protective device was in use, indemnity for the appliances is halved after applying the no-improvement standard. Diagnostic/reporting work is not a repair cost; a call-out is indemnifiable only when tied to work that is itself indemnifiable.

lines.invoice_text: Surge-damaged home electronics (speaker system and TV set)
lines.rationale: The two appliances are reported as physically damaged by the covered overvoltage event, so replacement with standard-grade equivalents is plausibly related and covered. The reasonable price is uncertain without model or specification details; the appliance sub-limit applies, and the missing protective device halves the otherwise payable amount.

lines.invoice_text: Diagnostic surge-failure report and technician call-out
lines.rationale: The reported attendance confirmed the cause and checked wiring safety, but the line describes no repair work on the damaged appliances; the diagnostic report is not a repair cost. The invoice’s covered equipment supply does not by itself make this separate diagnostic attendance indemnifiable, and three units are not plausible for a single reported visit.
